The first rune he cut glowed, and he spent a week trying to work out what he'd done right.

He worked it out, and his arms are proof.
background_sections.forward:
A rune nobody's ever cut before. He's filled three notebooks trying.

He's also looking for his brother, who was at school in Bogotá that day.
background_sections.now:
On the Ashen Reach, near the works, cutting runes into anything that'll hold still.

The tattoo machine grip on his hip is from his station at the shop, and he still cleans it every night.

recruits.look: Colombian man, 28, lean and athletic, black hair in a short fade with a longer top, light stubble, dark eyes, glowing rune tattoos down both forearms. Charcoal and electric-blue battle-wraps, a runed blade in each hand, a black and steel tattoo machine grip on a cord at his hip.

recruits.name: Emiliano Vargas
recruits.backstory: At the traffic lights in Oaxaca, Emiliano breathed fire for coins from car windows, two minutes a red light. He was good at it and very good at talking, and he arrived with a bottle of lamp oil on his belt. The fire here took to him at once. Now it comes out of him the colour of a dragon's breath, and he's cocky about it, and he's earned some of that.
recruits.greeting: Want to see a trick? I used to do this for coins at a red light. Now I do it for the Ashclaim.

background_sections.before:
A corner by the zócalo, four younger sisters, and a dream of a circus that would take him on.

In eleven years he didn't burn himself once, and he'll show you his hands to prove it.
background_sections.adjustment:
He says the Integration finally gave him the stage he wanted, and he only half means it.

The Ashclaim hired him the day he lit their forge from across the yard.
background_sections.forward:
A real show, in a real tent, with an audience that paid to get in.

He's also sending money home on every ship that leaves Cinderwharf, in case one of them finds it.
background_sections.now:
In Cinderwharf, by the forges, showing off to anyone who'll watch.

The bottle of lamp oil on his belt is the one he carried at home, and the label's nearly gone.

recruits.look: Mexican man, 29, slim and wiry, black hair a little wild, thin moustache, dark eyes, a cocky grin. Scarlet and gold pyromancer robes with dragon-scale trim and a draconic collar, a slim rod, a curl of flame at his lips, a plastic bottle of lamp oil with a faded label on his belt.

recruits.name: Isla Fraser
recruits.backstory: Isla stalked deer in the Highlands for the estates and shot biathlon for Scotland, and she's the stillest person you'll ever meet with a weapon in her hands. She stayed well clear of the Crusade. She joined the Order of the Pale Flame after Rory Callahan walked out of it, because she'd watched the Order do the work cleanly. She's sharp, level and quietly kind once the shooting stops.
recruits.greeting: I don't miss, and I'd rather not have to prove it today. Is there something you need?

background_sections.before:
A cottage above Glen Affric, the estate's deer, and a rifle she'd carried since she was fourteen.

She'd qualified for the World Cup the month before, and her dad had booked the time off to come.
background_sections.adjustment:
She went a year on her own, hunting what needed hunting in the Plaguelands.

The Order was the first group of people she met here who didn't waste a shot.
background_sections.forward:
She wants Stratholme cleared, properly, and she'll be there when it is.

She'd also like to hear her dad laugh again. She keeps that one to herself.
background_sections.now:
At Light's Hope Chapel with the Order's camp, keeping watch over the eastern road.

The steel buckle on her crossbow strap came off her biathlon rifle sling, and she's never thought about replacing it.

recruits.look: Scottish woman, 31, athletic and strong, long red hair in a thick braid, pale freckled skin, green eyes. A grey storm-coat over leathers with a white pale-flame pin, a heavy crossbow carried low, bolts at her hip, a worn steel biathlon rifle-sling buckle on her strap.

recruits.name: Dale Brekke
recruits.backstory: Dale farmed wheat outside Minot, North Dakota, on land his family had worked for four generations. He's big, slow-spoken and very hard to hurry, and he knows how to bring a harvest in before the weather turns. The scythe came naturally. He walks the plagued fields of the east now with it, and he says he's doing what he always did, which is clearing ground so something better can grow.
recruits.greeting: Bad ground out here, but it's ground. You'd be surprised what comes back if you give it time.

background_sections.before:
Two thousand acres, a combine he'd paid off the spring before, and a wife who ran the county co-op.

His kids were grown and gone to Fargo and Denver, and they called every Sunday after church.
background_sections.adjustment:
He took his time, the way he takes it with everything.

The first time he swung the scythe at something dead, he said it felt like the last pass of a long harvest.
background_sections.forward:
He wants to plant the Eastern Plaguelands one day, properly, with wheat that comes up clean.

He's been testing soil from every field he crosses and writing the results on the back of seed packets.
background_sections.now:
Out in the Eastern Plaguelands, working the fields one row at a time.

The seed-company cap tucked in his belt is the one he wore on the combine, and he puts it on when the work's done.

recruits.look: American man, 44, big and broad, sandy-brown hair cut short, short greying beard, blue eyes, a rugged sun-creased face. Dark brown and iron reaper plate, plain and practical, a huge two-handed scythe carried low, a seed-company cap folded into his belt.

recruits.name: Mohammed Saleh
recruits.backstory: Mohammed and his sister Layla ran a guesthouse in Aqaba, on the Red Sea, full of divers who came for the coral. He's warm, chatty and remembers every guest's name and how they take their tea. When they came through, he took the first job going, keeping the inn at Talrendis Landing, and then the dreams started: the same white street running into the sea, every night, with the queen's court walking it. Here the dreams turned into something he can use, and now he sees a little way along time, backward and forward.
recruits.greeting: Sit down, you look tired. Layla keeps the inn now, and I keep the dreams. Lately the dreams are the busier job.

background_sections.before:
Twelve rooms over a dive shop, a rooftop where the guests ate breakfast looking at Sinai, and a sister who did the books because he was hopeless at them.

He made the tea himself, every morning, and he never let a guest leave without a second glass.
background_sections.adjustment:
He kept doing what he knew, which was keeping people fed and rested, and it held him together.

The dreams frightened him until Farseer Thrag told him they were true. After that they mostly made him curious.
background_sections.forward:
He wants to walk the Drowned Promenade awake, once, and see if it looks the way it does at night.

Layla wants him to stop dreaming and help with the laundry. He says he can do both.
background_sections.now:
By the inn door at Talrendis Landing, with a glass of tea going cold beside him.

The brass key on a cord round his neck is the guesthouse's front door key. He still locks up at night, somewhere in his head.

recruits.look: Jordanian man, 41, medium build, warm brown skin, short dark curly hair going grey at the temples, a neat short beard, kind dark eyes with laugh lines. Deep teal and sand chronomancer robes with brass trim and a small hourglass at the belt, a staff with a glass orb full of slow-turning sand, a brass key on a cord round his neck.

recruits.name: Lúcia Ferreira
recruits.backstory: Lúcia ran a salon in Goiânia with two chairs, a radio that only got one station and a queue on Saturdays. Her grandmother raised her on rosaries and saints' days, and Lúcia still prays the way she was taught, out loud and with her whole heart. She's warm, chatty and a shameless gossip who never repeats a word said in her chair. Here the sun answers when she asks, which surprised her a lot less than it surprised the priests.
recruits.greeting: Sit down, sit down, you've got half the Barrens in your hair. I'll fix it while you tell me everything.

background_sections.before:
A pink-tiled salon on a busy street, a cat called Dona Flor and a mother who phoned every day at noon.

Her grandmother lit a candle every Sunday for everybody on their street, by name, and Lúcia kept the list.
background_sections.adjustment:
She landed with her scissors in her apron pocket. The first thing she did on this world was cut a grunt's hair, and he tipped her a copper.

She started praying at the Crossroads because she didn't know what else to do, and the light came down on the second day.
background_sections.forward:
A proper salon with a door that shuts and a mirror that isn't a bucket of water.

And a church, any church, where someone will sing with her.
background_sections.now:
At the Crossroads, by the inn, with a stool, a bowl of water and a queue of caravan guards.

She charges a copper and a blessing. Most of them pay the copper and pretend not to want the blessing.

recruits.look: Brazilian woman, 33, curvy, long dark-brown curly hair, warm golden-brown skin, large dark eyes. White and sun-gold cleric robes with a gold sun disc on the chest, a slim golden sceptre, hairdresser's scissors in a holster on her belt, a silver saint's medal on a chain.

recruits.name: Cristóbal Muñoz
recruits.backstory: Cristóbal was a wildfire brigadista in Valparaíso, and in 2024 he spent four days on the hills above his mother's house while the city burned. The house was still standing when he came down. He's brave, loud and reckless with himself but never with anybody else, and he calls everyone hermano within a minute of meeting them. Hellfire found him, which he says is a joke at his expense, and he's decided to laugh at it.
recruits.greeting: Hermano, you smell like smoke, which is good. It means you've been somewhere interesting.

background_sections.before:
A brigade station in the hills, a motorbike that broke down every week and a mother who sent him off with empanadas.

He danced cueca at every fiesta and was very bad at it, which he says is the point.
background_sections.adjustment:
He walked out of a grass fire on his first day, and he was the only one who walked out of it.

The fire inside him scared him for a month, and then he started using it to light other people's camps.
background_sections.forward:
Every town in the Barrens with a fire brigade of its own, and he's started training the first one.

His mother, Inés, knowing he's alive. He writes her a letter every week and keeps them all.
background_sections.now:
At Camp Taurajo, drilling a dozen young tauren on how to cut a firebreak.

When the grass goes up in the dry season, he's the one Taurajo sends for.

recruits.look: Chilean man, 35, athletic and broad-shouldered, thick black hair pushed back, a short dark beard, warm brown skin, dark eyes, soot on his face. Dark crimson and black knightly plate with orange hellfire in the seams, a two-handed flamberge, a yellow brigadista's helmet clipped to his belt.

recruits.name: Iker Etxeberria
recruits.backstory: Iker taught PE and coached pelota in Lekeitio, a Basque fishing town, at a school with a fronton wall older than the church. He's never met anyone he couldn't shout into running one more lap, and he's never been tired in his life. He's loud, upbeat and competitive about absolutely everything. Here the shouting turned into something real, and when Iker tells a fighter they can keep going, they really can.
recruits.greeting: Up, up, up! You can rest when you're dead, and you don't look dead to me.

background_sections.before:
A school of ninety kids, a fronton wall, a mother who made the best burnt cheesecake in the province, and an old bicycle he rode everywhere.

He lived above the bakery with Unai, a fisherman, for six years. Unai left at four in the morning and came back at noon, and Iker had the coffee ready.
background_sections.adjustment:
He landed in Arathi in the rain and started a running club for the farmhands within a week.

The first time his voice actually healed someone, he didn't notice. He just thought they'd been lazy before.
background_sections.forward:
A fronton wall in Arathi, and somebody here who plays properly.

And ninety names, written on a sheet in his pocket. The whole school was in session that day, and he doesn't know where any of them landed.
background_sections.now:
In Arathi West, with a whistle round his neck and a line of tired farmhands behind him.

They complain about him all day, and they've never been fitter in their lives.

recruits.look: Basque man, 33, strong and compact, dark brown hair short at the sides, clean-shaven, a strong nose and jaw, brown eyes. Bright steel guardian half-plate over a red and white padded coat, a round shield and a short sword, a coach's silver whistle on a red cord.

recruits.name: Héctor Salinas
recruits.backstory: Héctor wrestled lucha libre in Mexico City for fifteen years as El Relámpago de Plata, the Silver Lightning, and nobody outside his family ever saw his face. He's a showman with a huge laugh, superstitious about everything and much smarter than he lets anyone see. The trolls of Stranglethorn told him a mask is a spirit's face, and he said he'd known that his whole life. Now the spirits wear his, and the crowds at the arena love him.
recruits.greeting: Ah, a fan! Don't be shy. Everybody wants a picture with El Relámpago de Plata, even here.

background_sections.before:
Arena México on Friday nights, a gym in Tepito, a wife who sewed every mask he ever wore and two boys who wanted to be luchadores.

He retired a year before the Integration with a bad knee and a lot of good stories.
background_sections.adjustment:
He landed with his mask in his bag, and the first troll who saw it bowed to him.

A witch doctor at Grom'gol took him in, and he learned shadow and spirit the way he'd learned to fall, by doing it a thousand times.
background_sections.forward:
A real show in the arena, with rules, a ring and a crowd that cheers instead of waiting for blood.

And one day, his mask on his boys' faces. He's afraid he never will.
background_sections.now:
At the arena in Stranglethorn, signing autographs for goblins who can't read and posing for trolls.

He never takes the mask off his belt. He says a luchador who loses his mask loses his name, and he isn't taking chances.

recruits.look: Mexican man, 37, broad and powerful, short black hair and a sharp beard line, warm brown skin, dark eyes. Dark violet and bone witch-doctor robes with feathers and charms, a gnarled staff topped with a carved mask, a black luchador mask with silver flame trim on his belt.

recruits.name: Tobias Keller
recruits.backstory: Tobias worked on the Cologne Cathedral works crew, the team that's been repairing the cathedral for seven hundred years and will never finish. He replaced stones carved by men who died in the middle ages, and he loved it. He's patient, methodical and quietly devout, and he says very little, but all of it's true. The Light came to him the way good mortar sets, slowly, and it holds.
recruits.greeting: Mind the scaffold. That wall's coming along, but I'd rather you didn't lean on it yet.

background_sections.before:
A flat in the Südstadt, a crew of twelve who ate lunch together on the roof and a choir he sang bass in.

He carved a little face into every stone he ever replaced, somewhere nobody would ever look.
background_sections.adjustment:
He landed in the Plaguelands, which was very bad luck. The Argent Dawn took him in because he could fix a wall, and he's been fixing their walls since.

He found the Light on a scaffold, and he still prays best with a trowel in his hand.
background_sections.forward:
For Light's Hope to stand a thousand years, and to be the one who made it.

He'd also like to sing in a choir again. He's started one, and it has three people in it.
background_sections.now:
At Light's Hope Chapel, on the scaffold by the chapel wall, repointing mortar.

There's a little carved face on one of the new stones already. He won't say which one.

recruits.look: German man, 39, tall and broad, short light-brown hair, a neat short beard, grey-blue eyes. Polished silver paladin plate with a white tabard and a golden sun, a large kite shield and a mace, a stonemason's leather apron rolled at his waist with a chisel and mallet.

recruits.name: Camila Ortega
recruits.backstory: Camila worked in a lab in Durango, where the scorpions come into houses every summer, milking them for the venom that makes antivenom. She's done it ten thousand times, with tweezers and a steady hand. She's still, watchful and dryly funny, with nerves of steel, and she's fond of the things everyone else is scared of. Tanaris is full of scorpids, and she thinks it's the best place she's ever been.
recruits.greeting: Stand still, please. There's a scorpid under your boot, and it's having a worse day than you.

background_sections.before:
A lab with a thousand scorpions in jars, a flat over a bakery and a little sister who called her every night to complain about boys.

She saved a boy's life once, in the hospital next door, with antivenom she'd made that week.
background_sections.adjustment:
The first time a venomancer showed her what poison could do, she asked for the dose, the timing and the antidote, in that order.

She's very good at waiting for something to move, and here that's most of the job.
background_sections.forward:
An antivenom for every sting in Tanaris. She's already got six.

And news of her little sister, Daniela, and what she's doing now. Camila hopes it's something with boys.
background_sections.now:
In Northern Tanaris, sitting very still on a rock, watching the sand.

There's always a scorpid on her shoulder. It's never the same one, and it never stings her.

recruits.look: Mexican woman, 29, slim and lithe, long wavy dark-brown hair tied back, golden-tan skin, sharp dark eyes. Close-fitting dark green and black stalker leathers with a short hooded mantle, two curved daggers dripping green venom, an amber scorpion on her shoulder, lab safety glasses pushed up into her hair.

recruits.name: Sebastián Cruz
recruits.backstory: Sebastián ran the grill at a steakhouse in Palermo, in Buenos Aires, for twelve years, the one his grandmother ran before him. He knows meat, blood and fire better than anyone, and he's cheerful about all three. He's sociable, a born host and completely unbothered by gore, and he'll feed anybody who sits down. He landed in Tirisfal, among the Forsaken, and they find his blood magic deeply unsettling, mostly because he's so happy about it.
recruits.greeting: You look hungry, my friend. I've got something on the coals, and I promise it isn't anyone you know.

background_sections.before:
A parrilla with forty tables, a football club he'd die for and a grandmother who ran the kitchen before him.

Every Sunday he cooked asado for his whole family, twenty people, and he didn't sit down at his own table once. He's never noticed.
background_sections.adjustment:
The Forsaken don't eat much, which was the hardest thing he's ever had to accept.

Blood magic came easy, because he's been reading blood on a grill his whole life. He knows when it's ready.
background_sections.forward:
A grill in Brill that the living and the dead will both come to.

He's working on a recipe the Forsaken can actually taste, and he thinks he's close.
background_sections.now:
In Western Tirisfal, by a fire pit he dug himself, with a grill and a very worried farmer.

He waves at every passing Forsaken, and some of them have started waving back.

recruits.look: Argentine man, 34, lean and tall, dark brown hair swept back, a short neat beard, light olive skin, brown eyes. Deep crimson and black bloodmage robes with a leather apron over them, a slim rod with a blood-red crystal, a big carving knife in a sheath with a white cloth round the handle.

recruits.name: Enzo Marchetti
recruits.backstory: Enzo fenced sabre for Naples from the age of eight and came fourth at the Olympic trials, twice. Fourth is the worst place there is. He's proud, intense and charming when he wants to be, and he's honest with himself about what he traded. The Scarlets wanted his blade and he turned them down, because he'd seen what they do. A darker god offered more, and now he's the best swordsman he's ever met, and he's still deciding if it was worth it.
recruits.greeting: You're watching my feet. Good, that's where everybody should look. Most people look at the blade.

background_sections.before:
A salle in the Spanish Quarter, a mother who came to every bout and shouted at the referees, and a scooter that was always parked illegally.

He coached the little ones on Saturdays, and he was kinder to them than he ever was to himself.
background_sections.adjustment:
He landed with his fencing glove in his kit bag and nothing else. The Scarlets found him first, and then he found out what they were, and walked away.

The voice that offered him more didn't lie to him about the price, and he respects it for that.
background_sections.forward:
To beat the best blade on this world, fairly, in front of witnesses.

Then he'd like to know if he could've done it without the voice. He's afraid he already knows.
background_sections.now:
On the Scarlet Monastery Grounds, outside the walls, watching the Scarlets drill and finding the holes in it.

His white fencing glove is tucked in his belt. He doesn't wear it anymore, and he won't throw it away.

recruits.look: Italian man, 34, slim and athletic, short black curly hair, clean-shaven with a sharp jaw, dark eyes. Black and dark violet cultist battle-robes over close mail, a long single-edged curved blade with purple shadow along it, a white fencing glove tucked into his belt.

recruits.name: Taras Kovalenko
recruits.backstory: Taras took tourists into the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone for nine years. He walked them through Pripyat, past the school and the swimming pool, and every tour ended under the yellow Ferris wheel that had stood still since 1986. He's dry, morbid and very gentle with animals, and he crossed over with Kashtan, a Zone stray he'd been feeding at the checkpoint for years. When the wheel turned up in Deadwind, he was the first to volunteer, because he's the one person on this world who knows it by heart.
recruits.greeting: Stay on the path, please, and don't touch anything that glows. I've said that to a lot of tourists, and I've never meant it more.

background_sections.before:
A flat in Kyiv with a balcony full of his mother's tomatoes, and a minibus that smelled of instant coffee.

He knew every dog at every checkpoint by name, and they all knew his pockets had sausage in them.
background_sections.adjustment:
Kashtan settled in faster than he did. The dog found the first hunting trail in a week, and Taras followed him onto a witch hunter's road.

He told himself the wheel was a coincidence for about a day, and then he stopped telling himself that.
background_sections.forward:
To stand under the wheel one more time and work out why it came here when nothing else did.

Then he'd like to find a quiet village, a lot of dogs and nothing radioactive at all.
background_sections.now:
At the liquidators' camp in Deadwind Pass, checking everyone through the wash troughs at the gate.

He counts heads when people go out and counts them again when they come back. Kashtan won't set a paw where the ground's gone bad, and Taras has learned not to either.

recruits.look: Ukrainian man, 38, tall and lean, dark-blond hair cut short, light stubble, grey-blue eyes. A long dark grey witch-hunter coat over leathers, a wide-brimmed hat, a short crossbow and a hunting spear, a brown shepherd-mix stray at his heel, a yellow and black dosimeter badge on his collar.

recruits.name: Wes Dahlberg
recruits.backstory: Wes spent twenty years on the Hanford tank farms in Washington, cleaning up waste that'll outlive everybody who ever made it. He did it in a suit, by the procedure, with a partner, every single day. He's slow to speak and impossible to rattle, and he's the kind of man who reads the whole manual before he touches anything. Standing in front of something bad so other people don't have to is the only job he's ever wanted, so Deadwind suits him fine.
recruits.greeting: Suit check before you go past the fence. I don't care who you are, I check everybody.

background_sections.before:
A house in Richland with a boat in the driveway that he took out twice a year, and two daughters in college.

He coached his younger girl's softball team for six seasons and didn't raise his voice in all that time.
background_sections.adjustment:
The fighting came easy, because the shield works like the procedure does. You hold it, you don't panic and you don't step out of line.

The hard part was never knowing if his girls were all right, and he still doesn't know.
background_sections.forward:
The fallout boxed up, mapped and labelled, the way it should've been done at Hanford.

After that, a boat again. There's a lake in Ashenvale he's had his eye on.
background_sections.now:
At the liquidators' camp in Deadwind Pass, at the quarantine fence, checking suits.

The camp's mule follows him everywhere. He says he doesn't know why, and he feeds it apples.

recruits.look: American man, 46, very big and broad, sandy-brown hair cut short, a short greying beard, blue eyes. Heavy, scratched dull-steel plate, a big rectangular tower shield and a broad sword, a faded yellow hazmat hood rolled up through his belt.

recruits.name: Mariana Treviño
recruits.backstory: Mariana was a radiation therapist at a cancer centre in Monterrey. She spent her days lining up beams to the millimetre, so the radiation hit the tumour and nothing else. She's calm, precise and kind, with a gallows humour she only lets other medics see. She heals with the Light now, and she aims it the same way. When the liquidators asked for someone who wasn't afraid of the word radiation, she packed that night.
recruits.greeting: Come in and sit on the cot. I'll tell you what I'm doing before I do it, so nothing's a surprise.

background_sections.before:
Ten years on the same treatment floor, a running club that met at five in the morning and a brother who ran a taco stand by the stadium.

She remembered every patient's birthday and rang a little bell for them on their last day of treatment.
background_sections.adjustment:
She found the Light the way she'd found the right dose, carefully and with a lot of notes.

The priests in Orgrimmar said she prayed like an accountant. She took it as a compliment.
background_sections.forward:
She wants to keep a log of everything the fallout does to a body, so whoever comes next has something to work from.

She'd also like to run again one day, somewhere that doesn't glow.
background_sections.now:
In the infirmary at the liquidators' camp in Deadwind Pass, with a lamp and a stack of notebooks.

The Forsaken apothecaries bring her their worst cases, and they've stopped arguing with her charts.

recruits.look: Mexican woman, 31, slim, glossy black hair in a high ponytail, light olive-tan skin, warm dark-brown eyes. White and pale gold priest robes with a long open overcoat, a short staff with a glowing white crystal, a hospital ID badge on a teal lanyard.

recruits.name: Neil Hartley
recruits.backstory: Neil spent twenty years decommissioning the old buildings at Sellafield, on the Cumbrian coast, taking apart things that were never meant to be taken apart. He's dry, unflappable and pedantic about safety, and he makes truly awful jokes about half-lives. Fel fire came to him like a bad habit, and he treats it like everything else that's dangerous, with a lot of respect and a written plan. He's the calmest man in Deadwind, and he'd like everyone else to calm down as well.
recruits.greeting: Hard hat's optional, but I'd stand behind me if I were you. The green bit doesn't care whose side you're on.

background_sections.before:
A terraced house in Whitehaven, a season ticket for the rugby league and a wife who did the crossword in pen.

He walked the fells every Sunday and kept a list of every summit he'd done, in order.
background_sections.adjustment:
The first time fel fire came out of his hands he put it out, filled in a report and then tried again.

The warlocks found him maddening, because he wanted to know the dose of everything.
background_sections.forward:
He'd like to know what the fallout's made of, because nobody has asked the right questions yet.

He'd also like a proper cup of tea, and he's given up on that one.
background_sections.now:
At the liquidators' camp in Deadwind Pass, at the sample racks, labelling jars.

He's put up a sign by the pyre that says how long to stand near it. Nobody reads it, and he updates it anyway.

recruits.look: English man, 44, tall and fit, grey hair with some dark left in it, a neat short beard, green eyes. Black and iron felsworn robes over light plate with green fel runes, a staff with a caged green flame, a white hard hat with a reflective stripe hanging from his belt.

recruits.name: Valentina Soto
recruits.backstory: Valentina took tourists out into the Atacama desert at night to look at the stars, in Spanish, English and Portuguese. She always found the Southern Cross first and always cried a little when someone saw the Milky Way for the first time. She's bright, curious and a born teacher who gets lost in the sky. Here the stars answer her, and the druids of Moonglade have been teaching her what they mean.
recruits.greeting: Look up at it, really look. I've never seen anything like the sky over this lake, and I've seen a lot of sky.

background_sections.before:
A hostel in San Pedro de Atacama with a telescope on the roof and four dogs that belonged to nobody.

She was studying for an astronomy degree by correspondence, and she was two courses short.
background_sections.adjustment:
The first night she looked up, she didn't recognise a single star. She sat down and cried, and then she started drawing new charts.

By the end of the month the stars were answering her, and she's been fighting by their light since.
background_sections.forward:
She wants to finish her chart of this world's sky, all of it, and name the constellations properly.

She also wants to know if Earth's sun is up there somewhere, and she's afraid of the answer.
background_sections.now:
In Moonglade, out by the lake, where she can see the most sky.

She carries a little red torch so she doesn't ruin her night eyes, and she makes visitors use it too.

recruits.look: Chilean woman, 28, athletic and slim, long straight black hair over one shoulder, warm tan skin, dark almond eyes. Silver and night-blue warden armour, a long glaive with a crescent blade edged in starlight, a small red-lens torch on a cord round her neck.

recruits.name: Faris Al-Tamimi
recruits.backstory: Faris grew dates on his family's land along the Shatt al-Arab outside Basra, where the Tigris and the Euphrates meet. His grandfather taught him that you look after the water first and the palms look after themselves. He's gentle, patient and a very good listener, and he misses home with his whole body. The water spirits here took to him at once, and Moonglade's lake is the first water since home that he trusts.
recruits.greeting: Peace be with you. Sit by the water for a while, it's good water. I can tell.

background_sections.before:
Ninety palms, a house with a courtyard and a fig tree, and a big family that ate together every Friday.

He took his nephews out on the river in a flat boat and taught them the names of every bird.
background_sections.adjustment:
He woke in dry country, and for weeks he couldn't sleep without the sound of water.

A shaman found him at a spring talking to it, and told him the spring was talking back.
background_sections.forward:
Something planted here that'll still be standing in a hundred years.

He's been trying to grow a date palm from the stone of the last date he had in his pocket.
background_sections.now:
In Moonglade, by the lake, looking after the water and the people who come to it.

He keeps his grandfather's prayer beads round his wrist, and he turns them when he's thinking.

recruits.look: Iraqi man, 36, medium build and very fit, short black wavy hair, a close-trimmed beard, warm brown skin, dark eyes. River-blue and palm-green shaman mail and leathers, a wooden totem staff carved with fish and reeds, amber prayer beads round his wrist.
